Open Publishing or GTFO!

These companies are obstructing the advancement of science. They are holding hostage scientific research which was funded by public taxes. Elsevier should not exist.
If it was publicly funded, it should belong to the public, end of story. NO ONE should be allowed to profit off of limiting access to it.

I really think Journals need to realise that average citizens want quality information about the latest advancements in scientific fields. If they simply made the whole article free minus the data analysis we would be able to get quality* articles when we want and the people who actually do pay for them need the data, so the journal doesn't lose out.

*I'm going to ignore the debate on quality of modern journals.

Fuck them. I mean, seriously, fuck Elsevier. I'm a physician in private practice. I cannot count the number of times I needed more than the abstract of some shitty-ass article, and Elsevier wants me to pay $34 for 1-month access to their piece of crap, because I'm not affiliated with an institution.

Look assholes, I probably paid for half of that goddamn thing already, between the goddamn government grants the authors got and the amount of time I've had to listen to some damn industry rep jack off in my office when all I want to do is get the fuck home. So gimme the goddamn article already.

Jesus fucking christ. Those guys piss me off.

EDIT:   For anyone who has the capacity, please try to mirror - at least at your local machine - the libgen project. It is radically decentralized - at least in theory it should behave like a Hydra.   There was a huge dispute regarding Elsevier and it's business model in the mathematical community some years ago.

 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cost_of_Knowledge

 

https://gowers.wordpress.com/2013/01/28/the-elsevier-boycott-one-year-on/

 

Hearing that they push against the spread of knowledge is not a surprise. TL;DR:

 

The three reasons he cited for the boycott are high subscription prices for individual journals, bundling subscriptions to journals of different value and importance, and Elsevier's support for SOPA, the PROTECT IP Act, and the Research Works Act. Furthermore researchers were asked to pay for the a submission, the proof reading was based on reputation, and the copies for libraries were sold as a digital copy and "printing rights", so the library had to do that themselves. Complete and utter scum, if you ask me.

As a researcher this drives me utterly insane. Publishing companies have raised the price of institutional subscriptions so much that it's hard to find papers when I'm at a university. There just isn't a reason for a university to have enough subscriptions to cover all of the journals out there. Heaven forbid I'm consulting for a commercial entity or am reading up on something in my field for my own personal interest.

I'm all for supporting open publishing options. The community needs to push this. As it stands the researchers do a ton of the work including the review. Half the time when we get them back after the editor has seen them we have to fix things they messed, like units and notations. We can have peer reviewed journals that are open access.

These bastards were called out by Aaron Swartz by name, and take most of the responsibility for the closing of Gigapedia three years ago, to which Library Genesis has only recently caught up, imo. LG has until now benefited from the lack of US copyright enforcement in Russia, but that changed a few years back when the usual suspects started twisting Russian arms about VKontakte MP3 butthurt.

Supposedly there's a good torrent- or DC++-based means of setting up a Library Genesis mirror, but a lot of the important bits of the FAQ for that were only in Russian last time I looked ...
